reason: Base UI draws Checkbox and Radio as a span, so shadcn's disabled:opacity-50 (a :disabled selector) never matches and a disabled control stays fully opaque upstream; sera reads [data-disabled] instead, which is what the utility means. An upstream defect, not a sera value. Same as foundation's.

The preset is generated with rtl:false, so its paddings and radii are physical (pl-/pr-, rounded-l-) and do not mirror under dir=rtl; the layer-3 rules are logical. The section proves DirectionProvider renders, not a value. Same as foundation's.

A preset app's globals.css carries no .cn-* rules, so the cn-input-otp class the shadcn component keeps is unstyled there; style-sera.css's `.cn-input-otp { gap-2 }` is sera's own value and the system keeps it. Same as foundation's.

Upstream the Badge declares no line height of its own, so inside a text-sm Item it inherits the unitless 1.0204… of the surrounding type and resolves to 14.2857px. sera fixes line heights in px per type step (--badge-line-height reads --ui-line-height-xs, 15px), which is the whole point of the type axis: a badge is the same height wherever it sits. Layer 3 cannot win here — the only way to reproduce the inherited value is to drop the declaration (`initial`), which would make every badge in the system take its container's leading instead of the axis's. Exactly the same shape as foundation's `text-[0.625rem]` line-height row.

The shortcuts contain ⌘, which is in neither Noto Sans build: the reference app falls back through next/font's Noto Sans Fallback and the preview through Noto Sans Variable plus the Pretendard Hangul fallback, so the glyph advance differs by 0.3–1.8px. Font stack, not a value.
